target.outcome: Daily SUS hospital admissions with principal ICD-10 I21 (acute myocardial infarction)
target.pollutant: PM2.5, PM10, and nitrogen dioxide in a joint environmental cluster
target.geography: 39 municipalities of the São Paulo metropolitan region, Brazil
target.period: Reported as 2012–2015; reanalysis panel used 2012-01-01 through 2015-12-31
target.effect_scale: Difference in daily AMI admissions between hierarchical environmental clusters (reported 9% increase)

sources.role: health outcome: SIH-RD public DATASUS mirror, 2012-01 through 2016-04, SP

sources.url: not available: no credential-free source retrieved that provided all required daily pollutants

substitutions.published: DataSUS daily MI admissions; exact filtering details unavailable from supplied abstract/citation
substitutions.reanalysis: SIH-RD records with DIAG_PRINC beginning I21, admission date DT_INTER, and residence in the 39 RM São Paulo municipalities
substitutions.reason: This is the directly available public microdata implementation; it produced 51,689 admissions, not the reported 30,423, so equivalence was not assumed.

substitutions.reanalysis: 39 current RM São Paulo municipalities identified with IBGE codes and matched to SIH six-digit municipality stems
substitutions.reason: Article did not provide municipality codes/list in supplied material.

substitutions.published: Daily temperature variation, rainfall, humidity, NO2, PM2.5, PM10
substitutions.reanalysis: Open-Meteo daily temperature maximum/minimum, precipitation, and mean relative humidity at São Paulo city coordinate; pollutants unavailable
substitutions.reason: Independent archived weather was retrieved, but no complete credential-free public historical pollution series was retrieved.

substitutions.published: Hierarchical cluster analysis of six environmental variables, then admissions compared among clusters
substitutions.reason: All three pollutant variables are required for the published cluster definition; outcome total and clustered-day count also fail to reconcile.

coverage.notes: Outcome and weather are complete for every calendar day. SIH competence files through 2016-04 were read to mitigate billing lag, then deduplicated by AIH number and restricted to 2012–2015 admission dates. No pollutant days were available.

blockers: No independent, credential-free daily historical source providing PM2.5, PM10, and NO2 was successfully retrieved; clusters cannot be reconstructed with pollutants missing.

The supplied article says 30,423 patients and three clusters totaling 1,092 days, whereas the transparent 2012–2015 I21/residence extraction has 51,689 admissions and 1,461 days. The supplied materials lack sufficient methods to resolve this without silently changing the outcome/period.
Publisher full text was inaccessible: ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403 and the Elsevier API returned metadata only (openaccess=false).
